problemStatement.formal: Prove that D(n)/n! → 1/e as n → ∞, with the error bound |D(n)/n! - e^{-1}| ≤ 1/(n+1)!, where D(n) = numDerangements n.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the convergence of the derangement ratio D(n)/n! to 1/e with an explicit error bound using the alternating series estimation theorem.
whyMatters: Classic result connecting combinatorics (derangements) to analysis (exponential function)
Demonstrates alternating series estimation theorem in a concrete setting
The hat-check problem is one of the most famous problems in combinatorial probability

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: DerangementsConvergence.lean contains a full, sorry-free proof of the derangement convergence rate to 1/e. The main results are: (1) D(n) = n! × Σ_{k=0}^n (-1)^k/k! via strong induction on the recurrence; (2) e^{-1} = Σ_{k≥0} (-1)^k/k! connecting to NormedSpace.exp; (3) |D(n)/n! - e^{-1}| ≤ 1/(n+1)! via alternating series estimation; (4) D(n)/n! → e^{-1} via Metric.tendsto_atTop. The alternating series bounds are proved by even/odd case analysis with pairing of consecutive terms.

insights: The proof uses strong induction (Nat.strong_rec_on) to match the two-step recurrence D(n+2) = (n+1)(D(n) + D(n+1))
The connection to exp uses NormedSpace.exp (Banach algebra exponential) rather than Real.exp directly
Alternating series bounds are proved by pairing consecutive terms: 1/(m+2k)! - 1/(m+2k+1)! ≥ 0
The tsum splitting uses Function.Injective.hasSum_iff to reindex the tail
Convergence follows from the error bound + factorial growth, without needing epsilon-delta directly
